comments.author: pendantulum
comments.text: The small-angle approximation is doing a lot of unacknowledged work here. At the 12 degree swing shown in the video, the period correction term is about 0.3%, which is larger than the claimed final error. Either the author got lucky with cancellation or the webcam timing errors happen to lean the other way.

replies.author: smallangle
replies.text: OP here — not luck, and the handle should have been a hint. I fit the full elliptic-integral period expansion to the decaying amplitude, so the correction is applied per-swing as the pendulum settles. The webcam's rolling shutter was the actual villain; there's a whole appendix on it.

replies.author: pendantulum
replies.text: I stand corrected, and I clearly stopped reading before the appendix. The rolling shutter analysis is nicer than the pi estimate.

comments.author: lambdacurious
comments.text: There's a lovely genre of "measure a constant with junk-drawer equipment" projects and this is a strong entry. My contribution: estimating the speed of sound with two phones and a hallway. Got within 1.5% and a noise complaint.

comments.author: bitrotting
comments.text: Honest question: since g appears in the period formula, aren't you really measuring g and assuming pi, or measuring pi and assuming g? You can't extract both from one pendulum. The article hand-waves this by using the published local gravity value, which feels like smuggling in most of the answer.

replies.author: warmstart
replies.text: It's stated up front though — the point is the measurement pipeline, not metrological independence. By that standard no classroom experiment ever measures anything.
